title: Design an algorithm to serialize a binary tree to a string and deserialize that string back into the identical tree.
keyPoints: Serialization converts a tree to a flat string with explicit null markers to preserve structure
Preorder with null sentinels is fully reversible because markers tell the reader where branches end
Deserialization consumes tokens in the same preorder order using a queue or pointer
The delimiter must be unambiguous so multi-digit values are not merged into one token
Both operations are O(n) in time and space, processing each node and null marker once
Level-order serialization is an equally valid alternative used by LeetCode and many systems

s1_definition.oneliner: Write preorder with explicit null markers to serialize, and read the same preorder with those markers to deserialize into the identical tree.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Serialization** converts a binary tree into a flat string that captures both structure and values.
- **Null markers** (such as `#`) record the absence of children, making a single preorder traversal fully reversible.
- **Deserialization** splits the string into tokens and consumes them in the same preorder order to rebuild the tree.
- **Delimiter** (such as `,`) separates tokens unambiguously so multi-digit values are not merged.
- **Time** is O(n) in both directions; **space** is O(n) for the string and the recursion stack.
s1_definition.analogy: Rajesh needs to send the National Bank of India's approval hierarchy to another branch over a text-only channel. He writes it out as a single line: each manager's name followed by a comma, and a special placeholder wherever there is no one. On the other end, Priya reads that line in the same order and rebuilds the exact chart, because the placeholders tell her precisely where each branch ends.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Serializing and deserializing a binary tree is about making the tree's structure survive a flattening into text and come back identical. The key idea is to record the absence of children explicitly with a null marker. That single addition makes a preorder traversal fully reversible, because the markers tell the reader exactly where each branch terminates.

For serialization, you do a preorder walk writing each node's value followed by a delimiter and a sentinel for every null child. For deserialization, you split the string into tokens and consume them in the same preorder order using a queue: a value token becomes a node whose children are built recursively, and a null token returns null. The symmetry is the whole trick, because both directions process node, then left, then right.

Both operations are O(n) in time and space. In production, you would typically use JSON or Protocol Buffers, but the preorder-with-null-markers scheme is the clearest to implement and explain in an interview. Level-order serialization is an equally valid alternative and is how LeetCode displays trees.

At the National Bank of India, Rajesh used this to transmit and archive branch approval hierarchies. A branch serializes its hierarchy into a text field for the central system, and later the system deserializes it back for audits. The explicit null sentinels and a clear delimiter guarantee the round trip is lossless.

Remember one sentence: preorder with explicit null markers makes serialization reversible because the markers tell the reader exactly where each branch ends.
